name: Aldgate walking tour
description: A guided walk around the fascinating and often overlooked area of Aldgate in the City of London.

name: Andaz London Liverpool Street
description:
Andaz London Liverpool Street, a concept by Hyatt, blends rich history dating back to the 1200s with modern decor and the vibrant energy of its London neighborhood.

Step inside and join us for an open house tour led by our dedicated team!

name: Bethlem Royal Hospital
description: Guided walking tours of the grounds of Bethlem Royal Hospital, taking in the Hospital's historic Chapel, its beautiful grounds, the GUTS Cafe, Bethlem Museum of the Mind, and Bethlem Gallery.
address: Bethlem Museum of the Mind, Beckenham, BR3 3BX

name: Corbett Community Library
description: Visit the Grade II listed Corbett Community Library building. This beautifully preserved Edwardian building is rich in architectural character and heritage, featuring , an impressive dome, ornate door handles, some stained glass and a historic brass plaque. Discover the history and craftsmanship of this remarkable community landmark during your visit.
address: Corbett Community Library, 103 Torridon Road, SE6 1RQ

name: Croydon Urban Room
description: The Croydon Urban Room is a space to talk about the past, present and future of the Croydon town centre. Through conversa­tions, stories, exhibitions and events, the Urban Room brings together the views of those who live, work and visit the area to create a shared vision of the future and test new uses live in action.

name: Explore the authentically recreated Colony Room
description: A revival and love letter to London’s lost bohemia. Travel back in time to the legendary haunt of some of Soho's greatest creatives.   Featuring pictures, press cuttings and even the piano from the much loved private members club.

name: Fitzrovia Chapel
description: Loughborough Pearson's red brick building is unimposing from the outside, but inside is a riot of Gothic Revival design. Golden mosaics reveal the character of the Grade II* listed chapel, built as part of the Middlesex Hospital.

name: Flood Meadows at Hampton Court
description: A guided walk through Home Park Water Meadows with Thames Landscape Strategy. It is the site of a wetland restoration project that has increased biodiversity and sustainability on the historic site. It is not usually open to the public.
address: 1 Hampton Ct Rd, Hampton Wick, Molesey , KT1 4AE

name: Flux Innovation Lounge, Greenwich Design District
description: Flux Innovation Lounge opens its doors for Open House Festival, inviting visitors to explore where physical, virtual and immersive worlds meet. Described as one of London’s most celebrated creative venues and a hotbed for innovation and technology, Flux is a working innovation space where ideas are tested, experienced and brought to life. Join us to discover the future of the built environment.
address: Building B2 Unit 1, 1st Floor,, 1 Barton Yard, Soames Walk,, SE10 0BN

name: From Limehouse to Canary Wharf
description: Medieval industry, imperial trade, immigration, poverty, wartime destruction and modern regeneration have all left their mark on the Limehouse area. This walking tour covers a range of architects and architecture from C18th to C21st.

name: IMPACT Community Arts Centre
description: We are a theatre company for performers and artists with learning disabilities in the West London area. We will put on an exhibition of artworks and costumes at our Community Arts Centre.
address: Ealing Central Sports Ground, Horsenden Lane South, Greenford

name: Kenwood
description: A striking Neoclassical villa in tranquil gardens on Hampstead Heath, Kenwood boasts breath-taking interiors by Robert Adam and a world-class art collection.

name: King's Cross Masterplan
description: The Stirling-prize shortlisted King’s Cross Masterplan established a framework for the incremental redevelopment of this industrial heritage site through a mix of uses and a network of public spaces structuring new urban blocks and knitting the site into its context.
address: In front of Bird Cage sculpture, N1C 4TB

name: London National Park City Visitors Centre
description: London is the world's first National Park City, and our visitors centre at 80 Mortimer Street is the entry point to hundreds of places to visit and things to do across a greener, healthier and wilder London.

name: London Open Form Pavilion of Air
description: A floating acoustic architecture, playfully reframing public space as an essential community engagement through sound & site mapping. Accessed by smartphone, headphones & echoes.xyz app, the Pavilion is located outside the Serpentine Gallery,. Drawing on Oskar & Zofia Hansen’s Open Form architectural concept it is one of 15 in a series including Venice, Berlin, Dublin, Bergen and Arctic Norway.

name: Morris+Company | 'Waste Not: Materials, Making and the Circular Economy' Exhibition
description: Morris+Company is an award-winning architecture practice based in Hackney, east London. We have applied circular economy principles to the retrofit of our own studio, gallery and café space on Mare Street, reducing waste, reusing materials, and designing for longevity.  We place the creative ‘act’ of architecture onto the high street, reveal our practice to the public and engage local communities.

name: Parkland Walk
description: A walking workshop exploring the intersections of nature and urban space along Parkland Walk, a former railway transformed into London's longest local nature reserve. Through sensory and reflective exercises, participants will investigate ecological succession, green infrastructure, and the ways human and more-than-human worlds shape, reclaim, and coexist within the city.

name: Reimagining Play in London's Green Spaces
description:
An interactive workshop inviting residents and visitors to reimagine the public spaces around them using art and simple architecture techniques.

Open to children, families, and older residents, the workshop encourages intergenerational dialogue, bringing together youthful imagination and lived experience to explore the community's creativity.

name: Resonance FM Studios
description: Resonance FM is a pioneering, non-profit community radio station, with a studio at 7 Risborough Street, Southwark, London. Broadcasting 24/7 on 104.4 FM, DAB, and online, it offers over 100 weekly shows created by volunteer engineers and programme-makers. The station champions free expression and artistic diversity, providing a platform for local and international voices across arts & culture.

name: Royal College of Physicians
description:
Striking, provocative and one of London’s few Grade I listed post-war buildings – welcome to architect Denys Lasdun’s award-winning design. We invite you to drop in, take an expert tour, explore our archives and museum, get creative and more to discover the Royal College of Physicians' London home. 

See https://history.rcp.ac.uk/event/open-house-festival-2026 for more.
address: 11 St Andrew's Place, Regent's Park, NW1 4LE

name: Secrets and Symbols of the City
description:
A curious and enlightening wander through the City of London led by an expert guide. If you know where to look, the past still communicates its secrets concealed within a city that is 2000 years old.

We'll discover clues to the City’s past in strange marks and curious symbols along the route, keeping an eye out for honeybees, demi-maidens and sunbursts.
address: City Information Centre, St Paul's Churchyard, EC4M 8BX

name: Sinfonia Smith Square
description: A rare example of Thomas Archer's work and a masterpiece of English Baroque, originally dubbed Queen Anne's Footstool. A Grade I listed building, restored by Marshall Sisson after extensive bombing damage, now a busy concert hall.

name: Somers Town folk
description: Explore a fascinating working-class neighbourhood with a radical and surprising past. Learn of its efforts to hold onto its distinctive and proud culture in the face of rapid gentrification, especially within the neighbouring St Pancras and King's Cross districts. Discover the place of nature, community, heritage, and wellbeing in a neighbourhood that's changing very rapidly.
address: Concourse of the British Library, by the Sir Isaac Newton statue

name: Southbank Printmakers
description:
We are a friendly artist run gallery in Wells Street offering affordable, handmade fine art prints with a broad range of subjects created using many different printmaking techniques.
We aim to encourage people who have never encountered art before to experience printmaking through our regular workshops.

name: St Anne's Church Wandsworth
description: St Anne's Church, a SW London landmark, nicknamed Pepperpot, celebrated its bicentenary in 2024 (Robert Smirke 1824). The church will be open September 15, 17 and 18 for guided tours and exhibits from the archives.

name: St Anne's Church, Limehouse
description: St Anne's Limehouse has been described as 'the finest parish church in England.' Designed by Nicholas Hawksmoor, it is Grade I listed and one of the Major Churches in the Church of England. It is home to a thriving Christian congregation.

name: St Bartholomew's Hospital
description: The Grade I listed North Wing at St Bartholomew’s Hospital in the City of London houses two of England’s most important interiors, the Great Hall, and the Hogarth Stair with its large paintings by William Hogarth. The hospital was designed by architect James Gibbs and construction of the North Wing was completed in 1732.
address: St Bartholomew's Hospital, West Smithfield, EC1A 7BE

name: St Bride's Church, Fleet Street
description: Wren designed building of 1675, interior lost in blitz of 1940, reopened 1957 with 'Wren inspired' interior
address: St Bride's Church, St Bride's Avenue, EC4Y 8AU

name: St George's Cathedral
description: A stunning cathedral in the heart of London. Discover the story of a forgotten masterpiece. Designed by Augustus Pugin and opened in 1848, the original cathedral was hailed as England's foremost Catholic church before an incendiary bomb devastated the building in 1941. Explore the history, architecture and legacy that shaped the Cathedral you see today—and discover its remarkable story.

name: St James's Piccadilly
description: St James's Piccadilly is a Grade I listed Christopher Wren church in the heart of the West End. Completed in 1684, and known as the Artists' Church, its interiors include historic works of art by Grinling Gibbons (reredos, organ case and font), postwar Classical interiors by Albert Richardson, and contemporary art by Che Lovelace honouring the 18th-century abolitionist Quobna Ottobah Cugoano.

name: St Mary's Church, Battersea
description: During Open House, the Friends of Battersea Parish Church present a Floral Festival, organ recitals, historical displays, alongside 3 talks exploring history, creativity, sanctuary & Battersea’s radical past. Sat 12 Sept Dr. Peter Rumley at 6pm, Tues 15 Guy Stagg at 6.30pm,  Thurs 17 at 6.30pm Rory Walsh & Mike Squires.  Plus Join us for Choral Evensong amidst the flowers at St Mary’s Battersea.

name: St Pancras Church & Crypt
description: The church (1822 - Grade I listed) is an early and important example of Greek Revival architecture in London. Significant features include the caryatids and tower copied from models in Athens, and the atmospheric crypt.
address: Euston Road/Upper Woburn Place NW1, NW1 2BA

name: St Thomas with St Matthew, Clapton Common
description: Originally, built in 1773 as the Stamford Hill Chapel, St Thomas' are "Citizens with the Saints". The Heritage Lottery Fund, local artists, and academics are working with the church to engage and preserve how we work together as 'commoners' and 'caretakers for the 'common good'. Explore this in the Exhibition - On Common Ground - and become part of St Thomas' Future for the Common Good.
address: 1 Clapton Terrace, Clapton Common, Hackney, E5 9BW

name: Stamford Brook walk
description: Start at Stamford Brook tube.  Follow the hidden river, Stamford Brook, through streets and parks.  Amongst the architecture we will see on this route is a delightful square with great variety.  Finish near Hammersmith Station.

name: Suleymaniye Mosque
description: 6-storey building featuring a Western exterior and traditional Islamic interior, modelled on the Blue Mosque in Istanbul. Has dome and minaret tower.

name: The Photography Foundation Studio, Design District (D2)
description:
Come and see our light filled Studio & Office space and find out more about what we do at The Photography Foundation! 

Browse our Trainee photography zines and meet our welcoming Staff Members.
address: Building D2 (Level 2) 3 Dormer Yard, Design district, SE10 0EB

name: The Swedenborg Society
description: Grade II-listed Georgian domestic building c.1760, formerly part of the Bedford Estate. Interior refurbished 1925 to form lecture hall (restored 2014), library, bookshop and offices. Oak woodwork and green Doulton tiles line the staircase.

name: Walking Tour:  Charles I - Monster or Martyr ?
description: Walking tour of the sites of the last days of King Charles I and the legacy of the upheavals which cost him his life and still echo to this day.

name: Walworth Town Hall
description: The Grade II listed Victorian complex, originally built between 1865 – 1906, is one of London’s most iconic civic buildings. After a devastating fire in 2013, it was placed in the Heritage at Risk Register and closed. Now, after sensitive restoration by Feix & Merlin and General Projects, it reopens its doors. With a modern CLT extension that celebrates its former glory while embracing its future.
address: Walworth Town Hall, 155 Walworth Road, SE17 1RS

name: Willesden Jewish Cemetery
description: London's pre-eminent Victorian Jewish cemetery, now transformed into a heritage attraction. The "House of Life"  shares stories of a community and remarkable biographies through guided walks and events.
address: Willesden Jewish Cemetery, Beaconsfield Road, NW10 2JE

name: Worlds End Studios
description:
The building of Worlds End Studios started life as a factory manufacturing machines for commercial baking ovens; it burned down and the remains were used as the foundations of what we know today.
Two young architects found the ruined site in 1974. They wanted to create a community workspace geared toward designers, one of the first of its kind, in London.
